record.title: Tight cycle-partition conjecture for dense edge-coloured graphs
record.statement:
For $r\geq2$ and $\delta\in(0,1/2)$, let

$$
cp_r(\delta):=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\max_{G\in\mathcal{G}(n,r,\delta)}cp(G),
$$

where $\mathcal{G}(n,r,\delta)$ consists of the $n$-vertex $r$-edge-coloured graphs with $\delta(G)\geq(1-\delta)n$, and $cp(G)$ is the smallest number of vertex-disjoint monochromatic cycles partitioning $V(G)$. **Tight cycle-partition conjecture.** There exists $K>0$ such that, for all $r\geq2$ and $\delta\in(0,1/2)$,

$$
cp_r(\delta)\leq Kr\left\lceil\frac{r}{\log(1/\delta)}\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture would improve the paper's $\mathcal{O}(r\log r\lceil r/\log(1/\delta)\rceil)$ upper bound to the matching order suggested by the lower bound. It is known for $\delta=\Omega(1)$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Francesco Di Braccio and Viresh Patel, “Monochromatic cycle partitions of r-edge-coloured graphs with high minimum degree”, arXiv:2601.22117 (2026).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2008.00926](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.00926), [arXiv:1509.05539](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05539).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22117

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2026).

record.title: Tight tree-cover conjecture for dense edge-coloured graphs
record.statement:
For $r\geq2$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, let

$$
tc_r(\delta):=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\max_{G\in\mathcal{G}(n,r,\delta)}tc(G),
$$

where $\mathcal{G}(n,r,\delta)$ consists of the $n$-vertex $r$-edge-coloured graphs with $\delta(G)\geq(1-\delta)n$, and $tc(G)$ is the smallest number of not necessarily vertex-disjoint monochromatic trees covering $V(G)$. **Tight tree-cover conjecture.** There exists $K>0$ such that, for all $r\geq2$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$,

$$
tc_r(\delta)\leq Kr\left\lceil\frac{r}{\log(1/\delta)}\right\rceil.
$$

This is proposed as a stepping stone toward the corresponding cycle-partition conjecture. The source does not state a general resolution; it records stronger results in particular ranges, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Francesco Di Braccio and Viresh Patel, “Monochromatic cycle partitions of r-edge-coloured graphs with high minimum degree”, arXiv:2601.22117 (2026).

record.title: Karabegov’s conjecture on finite planar point configurations with three closest neighbors
record.statement: Let a finite planar point configuration be a finite set of points in the plane, where the closest neighbors of a point are the points minimizing Euclidean distance from it. **Karabegov’s conjecture.** Any finite planar point configuration in which every point has exactly $3$ closest neighbors must contain at least $16$ points. The conjecture concerns the minimum size of a finite planar configuration whose nearest-neighbor graph is 3-regular; the source exhibits a configuration with $16$ points, while the asserted lower bound is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Alexander Karabegov and Tanya Khovanova, “Minimal 3-regular Penny Graph”, arXiv:2602.01287 (2026).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01287

record.title: Bachman–Bao–Wu's coefficient-solubility conjecture for ternary cyclotomic polynomials
record.statement:
For an odd prime $p$, define

$$
M(p)\coloneqq\max_{q,r} A(pqr),
$$

where $q$ and $r$ range over primes. **Bachman–Bao–Wu's conjecture.** For every odd prime $p$ and every integer $h$ with $1\le h\le M(p)$, the equation

$$
A(pqr)=h
$$

is soluble for arbitrarily large primes $q$ and $r$.
This conjecture predicts that every coefficient value up to the maximum attainable value for a fixed odd prime $p$ occurs for arbitrarily large choices of the other two primes. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture is open.
record.source_name: Gennady Bachman, “On Heights and Diameters of Ternary Cyclotomic and Inclusion-Exclusion Polynomials”, arXiv:2602.07727 (2026).

record.title: Polynomial pivot-minor Ramsey number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $R_{\mathrm{piv}}(k)$ be the minimum $n$ such that every $n$-vertex graph contains an independent set or clique of size $k$ as a pivot-minor. **Pivot-minor Ramsey conjecture.**

$$
R_{\mathrm{piv}}(k) \leq \mathsf{poly}(k).
$$

This conjecture would imply the polynomial bound for the vertex-minor Ramsey number. It holds when the graphs are restricted to any proper pivot-minor closed class, but remains open for arbitrary graphs.
record.source_name: Ruben Ascoli, Bryce Frederickson, Sarah Frederickson, Caleb McFarland and Logan Post, “Almost all graphs are vertex-minor universal”, arXiv:2602.09049 (2026).

record.title: The maximum-running-time comparison conjecture for infection rules
record.statement:
Let $H$ be an infection rule, let $M_H(n)$ be the maximum running time over all starting graphs on $n$ vertices, and let

$$
M'_H(n):=\max\{\tau_H(G): G\text{ is an $n$-vertex $H$-percolating graph}\}.
$$

**Maximum-running-time comparison conjecture.** For all infection rules $H$,

$$
M_H(n)=\Theta(M'_H(n)).
$$

The theorem preceding this conjecture gives a comparison for $(2,1)$-inseparable infection rules up to a constant-factor change in the number of vertices, but the general comparison remains open.
record.source_name: David Fabian, Patrick Morris and Tibor Szabó, “Graph bootstrap percolation – a discovery of slowness”, arXiv:2602.12736 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12736

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

record.title: The polynomial-exponent limit conjecture for running times
record.statement:
Let $H$ be an infection rule and let $M_H(n)$ denote its maximum running time. **Polynomial-exponent limit conjecture.** The limit

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\log M_H(n)}{\log n}
$$

exists for every infection rule $H$.

The paper does not know whether maximum running times are approximately polynomial. Existence of this limit would assign every infection rule a well-defined polynomial growth exponent, including constant, logarithmic and intermediate regimes.
record.source_name: David Fabian, Patrick Morris and Tibor Szabó, “Graph bootstrap percolation – a discovery of slowness”, arXiv:2602.12736 (2026).

record.title: The bipartite extremal-separation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a bipartite graph, let $M_H(n)$ denote the maximum running time of the $H$-process, and let $\operatorname{ex}(n,H)$ be the Turán extremal number of $H$. **Bipartite extremal-separation conjecture.** For every bipartite graph $H$,

$$
M_H(n)=o(\operatorname{ex}(n,H)).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the gap between known lower bounds for bipartite infection rules and extremal-number upper bounds. The paper notes that an even stronger polynomial separation might hold, but that stronger claim is not included here.
record.source_name: David Fabian, Patrick Morris and Tibor Szabó, “Graph bootstrap percolation – a discovery of slowness”, arXiv:2602.12736 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2508.03835](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03835).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12736

record.title: The edge-deletion extremal upper-bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H$ be an infection rule with at least three edges, let $M_H(n)$ denote the maximum running time of the $H$-process, and let $\operatorname{ex}(n,H-e)$ be the Turán extremal number of $H-e$ for an edge $e\in E(H)$. **Edge-deletion extremal conjecture.** For every infection rule $H$ with at least three edges,

$$
M_H(n)\leq O\left(\min_{e\in E(H)}\operatorname{ex}(n,H-e)\right).
$$

This conjecture proposes a general extremal upper bound for maximum running times, beyond the bipartite setting. It remains open, as the paper states the claim as a belief following the discussion of bipartite extremal bounds.
record.source_name: David Fabian, Patrick Morris and Tibor Szabó, “Graph bootstrap percolation – a discovery of slowness”, arXiv:2602.12736 (2026).

record.title: The complex Banach–Mazur distance conjecture for ℓ₁ and ℓ∞
record.statement:
For $n\geq 1$, let $\ell_1^n(\mathbb{C})$ and $\ell_{\infty}^n(\mathbb{C})$ denote the $n$-dimensional complex sequence spaces, and let $d_{BM}$ denote the Banach–Mazur distance between normed spaces. **The complex Banach–Mazur distance conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 1$,

$$
d_{BM}\bigl(\ell_1^n(\mathbb{C}),\ell_{\infty}^n(\mathbb{C})\bigr)=\sqrt{n}.
$$

The paper notes that the upper bound is known in every dimension, while the lower bound would follow from the unimodular Spencer conjecture. The exact value was stated to be unpublished even for $n=2$, so the conjecture remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Tomasz Kobos and Marin Varivoda, “A Complex Analogue of Spencer's Six Standard Deviations Theorem and the Complex Banach-Mazur Distance”, arXiv:2602.12868 (2026).

record.title: Symmetry and Hankel structure of minimal matrices of fixed RSK shape
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition with $n$ parts, and let $M=(m_{i,j})_{1\le i,j \le n}\in\mathcal{M}_\lambda$ be a minimal matrix of shape $\lambda$. A matrix is **Hankel** when its entries depend only on the sum of their indices. **Symmetry and Hankel conjecture.** Every minimal matrix $M$ of shape $\lambda$ is symmetric,

$$
m_{i,j}=m_{j,i}\quad\text{for all }1\le i,j\le n,
$$

and is Hankel: there exists a sequence of integers $s_2,s_3,\dots,s_{2n}$ such that

$$
m_{i,j}=s_{i+j}\quad\text{for all }1\le i,j\le n.
$$

The conjecture extends the characterization of minimum-inversion permutations of fixed RSK shape to nonnegative integer matrices of the smallest possible size. It is proved in the paper for two-row partitions, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Nimisha Pahuja, “Minimal Inversions in Integer Matrices of Fixed RSK Shape”, arXiv:2602.14931 (2026).

record.title: Unimodality conjecture for atom counts in numerical power monoids
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a numerical monoid, and for $k,l\in\mathbb N$ let $\alpha_{k,l}(H)$ be the number of $k$-element atoms of $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{fin},0}(H)$ whose maximum is at most $l$. **Unimodality Conjecture.** For every $l\in\mathbb N$, there is an index $k\in\llbracket 0,l\rrbracket$ such that

$$
\alpha_{0,l}(H)\le\cdots\le\alpha_{k,l}(H)
$$

and

$$
\alpha_{k,l}(H)\ge\cdots\ge\alpha_{l,l}(H).
$$

Experiments are reported to support this unimodality assertion; the source does not state a proof or disproof.
record.source_name: Salvatore Tringali, “Power monoids and their arithmetic: a survey”, arXiv:2602.15754 (2026).

record.title: The least-atom principle for optimal hypercontractivity of finite probability spaces
record.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a finite set $\Omega$, and let $\lambda\in(0,1/2)$ be the mass of its least atom. For $1<p<q<\infty$, let $\sigma_{p,q}(\mu)$ be the optimal constant for the operator $\mathbb{E}_\mu+r(\operatorname{Id}-\mathbb{E}_\mu)$ from $L^p(\mu)$ to $L^q(\mu)$, and let $\sigma_{p,q}(\lambda)$ denote the corresponding constant for the biased Bernoulli measure of parameter $\lambda$.

**Least-atom principle.** For all $1<p<q<\infty$,

$$
\sigma_{p,q}(\mu)=\sigma_{p,q}(\lambda).
$$

This asserts that the optimal constant depends only on the smallest atom of the finite probability space. It is motivated by numerical simulations and the cited result of Wolff, but the supplied text does not establish it for the full range $1<p<q<\infty$.
record.source_name: Jie Cao, Shilei Fan, Yong Han, Yanqi Qiu and Zipeng Wang, “The optimal hypercontractive constants for Z_3 and biased Bernoulli random variables”, arXiv:2602.17248 (2026).

record.title: The visibility-dimension claim for the abelian surface 9603.2.a.o
record.statement:
Let $A/\mathbb{Q}$ be the abelian surface with label $\textnormal{\texttt{9603.2.a.o}}$. Its Tate--Shafarevich group $\Sha(A/\mathbb{Q})$ contains an element of order $7$.

**Visibility-dimension claim.** This element is not visible in any abelian threefold; in particular, its visibility dimension is $4$.

This claim concerns the minimum dimension of an abelian variety over $\mathbb{Q}$ that makes a given element of the Tate--Shafarevich group visible. The supplied text gives no evidence that the claim has been resolved.

record.title: Spectral characterization conjecture for the 2-core of a sparse random graph
record.statement: Let $G(n,p)$ be an Erdős–Rényi graph with $p=\lambda/n$, let $C_{\textnormal{giant}}$ denote its largest component, and let $\operatorname{Core}_2(C_{\textnormal{giant}})$ be the graph obtained by removing all pendant trees. A graph is **characterized by its spectrum** if every graph with the same adjacency-spectrum is isomorphic to it. **The 2-core spectral characterization conjecture.** For every $1<\lambda\leq n/2$ that remains bounded away from one as $n\to\infty$, the $2$-core of the giant is characterized by its spectrum with probability tending to one. The conjecture proposes that pendant trees are the relevant obstruction to spectral characterization in this sparse regime; the paper presents theoretical and numerical evidence, while the assertion itself remains open.
record.source_name: Nils Van de Berg and Alexander Van Werde, “Are sparse graphs typically determined by their spectrum?”, arXiv:2602.22757 (2026).

record.title: The three-tree separation conjecture for bounded-degree trees
record.statement:
For integers $r\geq 2$, let $f(r,3)$ denote the limiting maximum proportion of vertices that can be guaranteed in each of two disjoint subsets separated by a cut vector for any three trees with a common vertex set labeled by $[n]$ and maximum degree at most $r$. **Three-tree separation conjecture.**

$$
f(r,3)=\frac{r-1}{r^3}
$$

This conjecture extends the known formulas $f(r,1)=1/r$ and $f(r,2)=1/(2r)$, and agrees with the proved value $f(3,3)=2/27$. The general case for three trees remains open.
record.source_name: Sagi Snir and Raphael Yuster, “Simultaneous separation in bounded degree trees”, arXiv:2602.23096 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23096

record.title: Colourful almost-spanning tree embedding conjecture for Dirac graphs
record.statement: Let $c$ satisfy $1/2<c\leqslant1$, and let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree $\delta(G)\geqslant cn$. **Colourful tree embedding conjecture.** There exists a constant $d>0$ such that, for every tree $T$ on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta(T)\leqslant dn/\log n$, every proper edge-colouring of $G$ contains a copy of $T$ using at least $cn-o(n)$ distinct colours. The conjecture is a colourful analogue of bounded-degree tree-embedding results for Dirac graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution evidence, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Xinbu Cheng, Xinqi Huang, Hong Liu, Bin Wang and Zhifei Yan, “Colour diversity in spanning structures under Dirac-type conditions”, arXiv:2602.23801 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23801

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2026). “This conjecture was disproved by Maamoun and Meyniel , who constructed infinitely many counterexamples.”

record.title: Caputo's hypergraph conjecture for symmetric-group representations
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma=([n],w)$ be a weighted hypergraph on $[n]$, with non-negative weights, and let $\rho$ be a non-trivial irreducible representation of $\mathrm{Sym}(n)$. Write $\pi_{(n-1,1)}$ for the standard representation minus the trivial representation, and let $\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\rho)$ denote the smallest eigenvalue associated with $\rho$. **Caputo's hypergraph conjecture.** For every such $\Gamma$ and $\rho$, 

$$
\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\pi_{(n-1,1)})\leq\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\rho).
$$

This generalizes the known theorem for measures supported on transpositions. The conjecture is still open in general.
record.source_name: Gil Alon and Doron Puder, “Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups”, arXiv:2603.00353 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00353

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026). “Conjecture is still open in general.”

record.title: Aldous–Caputo-type conjecture for the spectral gap of $\mathrm{U}(n)$
record.statement: Let $\Gamma=([n],w)$ be an arbitrary hypergraph with non-negative weights. For each irreducible representation $\rho$ of $\mathrm{U}(n)$, let $\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\rho)$ denote the smallest eigenvalue in its spectrum, and exclude the trivial representation. **Aldous–Caputo-type conjecture.** The smallest non-trivial eigenvalue of the $\mathrm{U}(n)$-spectrum of $\Gamma$ is attained in one of the irreducible representations $(1,0,\ldots,0,-1)$ or $(2,0,\ldots,0,-2)$. The conjecture extends the preceding theorem from hypergraphs of restricted support to arbitrary weighted hypergraphs; the source reports supporting results and computer simulations, but does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Gil Alon and Doron Puder, “Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups”, arXiv:2603.00353 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for new KMP eigenvalues
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a hypergraph with non-negative weights. For every $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, let $\omega_k=\omega_k(\Gamma)$ denote the smallest new eigenvalue of the Laplacian $\mathcal{L}(\Gamma,\mathcal{KMP}_k)$, meaning the smallest eigenvalue arising in the new invariant subspace at level $k$. **Monotonicity conjecture for new KMP eigenvalues.** 

$$
\omega_1\leq\omega_3\leq\omega_5\leq\cdots\qquad\text{and}\qquad\omega_2\leq\omega_4\leq\omega_6\leq\cdots.
$$

The inequalities are supported by computer simulations and generalize the proved result for hypergraphs supported on subsets of size $n-1$. The source gives no resolution in general.
record.source_name: Gil Alon and Doron Puder, “Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups”, arXiv:2603.00353 (2026).

record.title: Strong Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for simple digraphs
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tournament, let $D$ be a simple digraph on $n$ vertices with no subdigraph isomorphic to $T$, and let $\vec{\alpha}(D)$ denote its largest acyclic set. **Strong Erdős–Hajnal conjecture.** For every tournament $T$ there exists $\varepsilon_T>0$ such that

$$
\vec{\alpha}(D)\geq n^{\varepsilon_T}.
$$

This strengthens the tournament Erdős–Hajnal conjecture from oriented tournaments to arbitrary $T$-free simple digraphs. The paper gives an upper bound $\varepsilon_T\leq 2/t$ when $T$ has $t\geq3$ vertices, while the general conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Ararat Harutyunyan, Colin McDiarmid and Gil Puig i Surroca, “Acyclic sets and colorings in digraphs under restrictions on degrees and cycle lengths”, arXiv:2603.02947 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02947

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2026). “It was proved by Neumann-Lara that if $D$ is an oriented graph only containing odd cycles or only containing even cycles then $\vec{\chi}(D) \leq 2$.”

record.title: Vertex-minimality conjecture for the triangulation of real projective 5-space from \mathcal{P}_{6,48}
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}_{6,48}$ be the centrally symmetric simplicial $6$-polytope whose antipodal quotient of the boundary gives a triangulation of $\mathbb{R}P^5$. A triangulation is **vertex minimal** if no triangulation of the same space has fewer vertices. **Vertex-minimality conjecture.** The triangulation of $\mathbb{R}P^5$ obtained by antipodally identifying the boundary of $\mathcal{P}_{6,48}$ is vertex minimal among all triangulations of $\mathbb{R}P^5$. The construction has $24$ vertices, and the conjecture asserts that this is the fewest possible; at minimum, the authors expect minimality among triangulations arising from antipodally identifying a centrally symmetric polytope.
record.source_name: Dan Guyer, Stefan Steinerberger and Yirong Yang, “An Efficient Triangulation of RP^5”, arXiv:2603.07808 (2026).

record.title: Sharpness conjecture for k-hyperseparating set systems
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $V$ be an $n$-element set, and let $f(n,k)$ denote the smallest size of a $k$-hyperseparating set system on $V$. A set system is **$k$-hyperseparating** if, for every $v\in V$, there are sets $A_1,\dots,A_k$ whose membership pattern distinguishes $v$ from every other element of $V$. **Sharpness conjecture.** For any $k$, if $n$ is sufficiently large, then

$$
f(n,k)=\min \left\\{m:\binom{m}{k}\ge n\right\\}.
$$

The proposition preceding the conjecture gives the upper bound $f(n,k)\leq\min \\{m:\binom{m}{k}\ge n\\}$ and a lower bound differing by a factor involving $2^k$. The conjecture asserts that the natural construction from $k$-hypercompletely separating systems is optimal for sufficiently large underlying sets.
record.source_name: Dániel Gerbner, “A note on hyperseparating set systems”, arXiv:2603.08123 (2026).

record.title: The skewed coloring sampling conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\vec{n}=(n_1,\ldots,n_q)$ satisfy $\|\vec{n}\|_1=n$. An $\vec{n}$-coloring is a proper coloring with exactly $n_i$ vertices of color $i$.

**Skewed sampling conjecture.** There should be a polynomial-time algorithm that approximately samples uniformly from the set of $\vec{n}$-colorings of $G$ whenever

$$
n_i\leq\left\lfloor\dfrac{n}{2\Delta}\right\rfloor
$$

for every $i\in[q]$.

The paper presents this as a possible first step toward sampling substantially more skewed colorings, requiring new ideas; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Aiya Kuchukova, Will Perkins and Xavier Povill, “Sampling Colorings with Fixed Color Class Sizes”, arXiv:2603.08259 (2026).

record.title: The phase-transition conjecture for minima of $sigma$-Brjuno functions
record.statement:
Let $B_\sigma:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ be the $\sigma$-Brjuno function, and let $\eta_n=(\sqrt{n^2+4}-n)/2$ be the $n$-th fixed point of the Gauss map. For each $n\in\mathbb N$, consider the minimum of $B_\sigma$ on $[0,1]$. **Phase-transition conjecture.** For all $n\in\mathbb N$, there exists a value $\sigma_n^*\in(n-1,n)$ such that

$$
\min_{x\in[0,1]}B_\sigma(x)=
\begin{cases}
B_\sigma(\eta_n)&\text{if }\sigma\in[n-1,\sigma_n^*)\\
B_\sigma(\eta_{n+1})&\text{if }\sigma\in[\sigma_n^*,n].
\end{cases}
$$

Numerical evidence suggests that the minimizer remains locked at successive fixed points of the Gauss map and jumps between them at the critical thresholds $\sigma_n^*$; proving this description and the existence of these thresholds remains open.
record.source_name: Ayreena Bakhtawar, Carlo Carminati and Stefano Marmi, “On the minimum of σ-Brjuno functions”, arXiv:2603.08378 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08378

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

record.title: The path-graph variational constant conjecture
record.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathbf{C}_{P_n}$ denote its optimal $1$-variational constant, namely the smallest constant such that

$$
\textup{Var} M_{P_n}f\leqslant \mathbf{C}_{P_n}\textup{Var} f
$$

for every real-valued function $f$ on $P_n$.

**Path-graph conjecture.** For every integer $n\geqslant3$,

$$
\mathbf{C}_{P_n}=1-\frac1n.
$$

The source reports numerical evidence for all $n\leqslant10$. The conjecture would imply the bound $\mathbf{C}_{\mathbb{Z}}\leqslant1$ for the integer lattice, and hence the corresponding real-line bound, but it remains open and is expected to be difficult.
record.source_name: Cristian González-Riquelme, Vjekoslav Kovač and José Madrid, “Sharp variational inequalities for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on finite undirected graphs”, arXiv:2603.12462 (2026).

record.title: Cross-ratio rigidity conjecture for surfaces in \mathcal{S}
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{R}$ and $\mathcal{R}'$ be two surfaces in $\mathcal{S}$. Suppose the cell of $\mathcal{R}$ at position $(i,j)$ has cross ratio $k_{i,j}$, while the cell of $\mathcal{R}'$ at position $(i,j)$ has cross ratio $k'_{i,j}$. Assume that $k_{i,j}=k'_{i,j}$ for all $i,j$. **Cross-ratio conjecture.** Then $\mathcal{R}$ and $\mathcal{R}'$ have the same conformal type; equivalently, they are equivalent up to biholomorphism. This would show that the cross ratios determine the conformal type of a surface and would facilitate constructing probability distributions on the full space of surfaces with a square grid net, potentially advancing the study of parabolicity.

record.title: The abelian sandpile minimizes average density
record.statement:
Let $G=(V\cup\{s\},E)$ be a finite graph with designated sink vertex $s$, and let $\rho_G(p)$ denote the stationary average density for the $p$-toppling rule, where $p\in[0,1]$ and $p=1$ gives the abelian sandpile model. **Minimum attained by abelian sandpiles.** For all $p\in[0,1)$,

$$
rho_G(p)>\rho_G(1).
$$

This is the weaker statement that the abelian sandpile model has the smallest average density; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: David Beck-Tiefenbach and Robin Kaiser, “Stochastic Sandpiles with Uniform Toppling Rule on the Line”, arXiv:2603.16304 (2026).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.16304

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

record.title: Linial's path-partition conjecture for digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph and let $k$ be a positive integer. The $k$-norm of a path partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $D$ is $|\mathcal{P}|_k=\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}}\min\{|V(P)|,k\}$. A path partition is $k$-minimum when its $k$-norm is minimum, and this minimum is denoted by $\pi_k(D)$. A partial $k$-coloring is a collection of $k$ vertex-disjoint stable sets; let $\alpha_k(D)$ be the maximum number of vertices covered by such a coloring.

**Linial's conjecture.** For every digraph $D$ and every positive integer $k$,

$$
\pi_k(D)\leq\alpha_k(D).
$$

This extends the Gallai–Milgram inequality $\alpha_1(D)\geq\pi_1(D)$ and is one of Linial's two proposed generalizations involving $k$-optimal path partitions and colorings. The source states that the conjecture remains open.

record.title: Lee's polynomial anticoncentration conjecture for random spanning trees
record.statement:
Let $d$ be sufficiently large, let $G$ be a connected graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree at least $d$, and let $\mathcal{T}$ be a uniformly random spanning tree of $G$.

**Lee's conjecture.** For every tree $T$,

$$
\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{T} \cong T) \le n^{-\Omega(1)}.
$$

This conjecture seeks a polynomial anticoncentration bound in graphs of large minimum degree, generalizing the exponential anticoncentration known for almost regular graphs. The complete bipartite graph $K_{d,n-d}$ shows that an exponential bound in $n$ is impossible in this setting.
record.source_name: Veronica Bitonti, Lukas Michel and Alex Scott, “Anticoncentration of random spanning trees in graphs with large minimum degree”, arXiv:2603.17630 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17630

record.title: The sharp anticoncentration conjecture for random spanning trees
record.statement:
Let $d$ be sufficiently large, and let $n$ be sufficiently large relative to $d$. Suppose that $G$ is a connected graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree at least $d$, and let $\mathcal{T}$ be a uniformly random spanning tree of $G$.

**Sharp anticoncentration conjecture.** For every tree $T$,

$$
\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{T} \cong T) \le n^{-(1/2-o_n(1))(d-1)}.
$$

The conjecture proposes the optimal constant factor in the exponent and matches the anticoncentration scale suggested by the complete bipartite graph $K_{d,n-d}$. The paper proves a weaker anticoncentration bound, so this sharper estimate remains open.

record.title: Burr–Erdős–Graham–Sós maximal anti-Ramsey conjecture for odd cycles
record.statement:
Let $f(n,e,H)$ be the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of an $n$-vertex graph with at least $e$ edges such that every copy of $H$ is rainbow. Let $C_{2k+1}$ denote the cycle of length $2k+1$.

**Burr–Erdős–Graham–Sós conjecture.** For every integer $k\ge 3$,

$$
f\left(n,\left\lfloor \frac{n^2}{4} \right\rfloor+1,C_{2k+1}\right)=\frac{n^2}{8}+o(n^2).
$$

The conjecture asks for the precise quadratic asymptotics of the maximal anti-Ramsey function just above the Turán number of an odd cycle. The corresponding function is constant for triangles, linear for $5$-cycles, and quadratic for all longer odd cycles; the conjectured leading constant remains open according to the supplied status evidence.
record.source_name: Matija Bucic, Kaizhe Chen and Jie Ma, “On a maximal anti-Ramsey conjecture of Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Sós”, arXiv:2603.18952 (2026).

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026).

record.title: The unitary dual conjecture for general connected reductive groups
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero, and let $G$ be a general connected reductive group defined over $F$. Let $\Pi_A(G)$ denote the set of Arthur representations, and let $\Pi_{\overline{A}}^{\lim}(G)$ be the set obtained from them by unitary parabolic induction, complementary series, and limits of complementary series. Assume that the local Arthur conjecture holds for every Levi subgroup $M$ of $G$. **Unitary dual conjecture.** The two sets are equal:

$$
\Pi_{\overline{A}}^{\lim}(G)=\Pi_u(G).
$$

This conjecture seeks to construct the entire unitary dual from Arthur representations using the standard unitary constructions; its resolution is not established by the supplied text.
record.source_name: Baiying Liu, Chi-Heng Lo and Brian Wen, “On corank 4 unitary representations of classical groups”, arXiv:2603.22255 (2026).

record.title: Brešar–Klavžar–Rall–Wash conjecture on subdivisions of subcubic graphs
record.statement: For a graph $G$, its **1-subdivision** is obtained by replacing every edge with a path of two edges. The packing chromatic number $\chi_p(G)$, or PCN, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ has a packing $(1,2,\ldots,k)$-coloring. **Brešar–Klavžar–Rall–Wash conjecture.** The $1$-subdivision of every subcubic graph has PCN at most $5$. Many advances have been made toward this conjecture, but the supplied status evidence says that it remained open since 2016.
record.source_name: Xinmin Hou, Xujun Liu and Xiangyang Wang, “Every connected subcubic graph except the Petersen graph is packing (1,1,2,2)-colorable”, arXiv:2603.23434 (2026).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23434

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026). “Many progresses has been made toward Question and Conjecture , but it still remains open since 2016.”

record.title: The projection-area conjecture for three-dimensional cube dismantling
record.statement:
Let $[n]^3$ be the $n\times n\times n$ cube, and let $s_3(n)$ denote the minimum possible area covered by the three orthogonal projections onto the faces of a solution to the faces of $[n]^3$. **Projection-area conjecture.**

$$
s_3(n)\ge n^2+6n-4
$$

for all $n$. The conjecture, attributed in the source to Hjorth et al., asserts that the solution whose black cubes lie in three orthogonal facial sections achieves the minimum projection area.
record.source_name: János Barát and Ian M. Wanless, “A cube dismantling problem related to bootstrap percolation”, arXiv:2603.23913 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23913

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026). “The first class of open questions involves trying to make consecutive moves from neighbouring vertices, so that the sequence of moves form a path.”

record.title: The minimum-codegree conjecture for squares of tight Hamilton cycles in 3-graphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a $3$-graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\delta_2(H)$ denote its minimum codegree, the minimum number of vertices completing a pair to an edge of $H$. The **square of a tight Hamilton cycle** is the spanning $3$-graph obtained by taking every triple contained in four consecutive vertices of a cyclic ordering. **Minimum-codegree conjecture.** For every $\alpha>0$ there exists $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every $3$-graph $H$ on $n\geq n_0$ vertices with

$$
\delta_2(H) \geq (3/4+\alpha)n
$$

contains the square of a tight Hamilton cycle. This conjecture improves the sufficient bound proved in the paper from $7n/9+o(n)$ toward the expected threshold $3n/4$. The source describes it as a highly significant open problem in extremal graph theory.
record.source_name: Debmalya Bandyopadhyay, Allan Lo and Richard Mycroft, “Towards Pósa's Conjecture for 3-graphs”, arXiv:2603.28202 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28202

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026).

record.title: The exact extremal number of $C_4$-free subgraphs of $Q_8$
record.statement:
Let $Q_8$ be the 8-dimensional hypercube and let $C_4$ denote the cycle of length four. Write $\mathrm{ex}(Q_8,C_4)$ for the maximum number of edges in a subgraph of $Q_8$ containing no copy of $C_4$. **The $Q_8$ extremal conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{ex}(Q_8,C_4)=680.
$$

A 680-edge $C_4$-free subgraph is constructed and certified, and every non-edge creates a $C_4$ when added. The equality is not established because the reported computational search for 681 edges found no $C_4$-free example.
record.source_name: Minamo Minamoto, “New Lower Bounds for C4-Free Subgraphs of the Hypercubes Q6, Q7, and Q8: Constructions, Structure, and Computational Method”, arXiv:2603.29127 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: The exact extremal number of $C_4$-free subgraphs of $Q_7$
record.statement:
Let $Q_7$ be the 7-dimensional hypercube and let $C_4$ denote the cycle of length four. Write $\mathrm{ex}(Q_7,C_4)$ for the maximum number of edges in a subgraph of $Q_7$ containing no copy of $C_4$. **The $Q_7$ extremal conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{ex}(Q_7,C_4)=304.
$$

A 304-edge $C_4$-free subgraph is constructed and certified, with extensive computational evidence from independent searches that no 305-edge example was found. The exact upper bound remains unproved in the supplied text.

record.title: The Golomb return conjecture for threshold positions
record.statement:
Let $G$ be Golomb's sequence, let $S(k)=\sum_{n=1}^{k}G(n)$, and let $N_r(n)$ denote the relevant multiplicity for order $r$; define $M(r)=\sup_n N_r(n)$. For each $k$, let $j_k$ be the smallest order $r$ at which $M(r)$ first reaches $k$. **Golomb return conjecture.** For all $k\ge 4$, 

$$
j_{k+1}-j_k=G(k)\qquad\text{and}\qquad j_k=S(k-1)+2.
$$

This conjecture describes the observed Golomb-sequence structure of the threshold positions $j_k$. A complete proof remains open; the paper reduces it to two boundary conjectures.
record.source_name: Benoit Cloitre, “Almost Golomb Sequences”, arXiv:2604.02404 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02404

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2026). “While a complete proof of Conjecture remains open, the phenomenon can be reduced to two precise boundary conjectures.”

record.title: Fill's multiplicity conjecture for minimizing adjacent-transposition walks
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 3$ and let $\vec{p}$ be a regular parameter vector. A label is **neutral** if $p_{c,i}=p_{i,c}=1/2$ for every $i\neq c$. Let

$$
N(\vec{p})=\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft|\{i\in[n]:i\text{ is neutral}\}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright|
$$

be the number of neutral labels, and let $M(\vec{p})$ be the algebraic multiplicity of $1-\lambda_*$ in $\operatorname{spec}(K(\vec{p}))$, where $\lambda_*$ is the uniform parameter vector's spectral gap. **Fill's multiplicity conjecture.** If $N(\vec{p})\notin\{n-2,n\}$, then

$$
N(\vec{p})=M(\vec{p}).
$$

If $N(\vec{p})\in\{n-2,n\}$, then

$$
M(\vec{p})=n-1.
$$

This conjecture concerns the multiplicity of the second largest eigenvalue in the conjectured equality cases and remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Vishesh Jain and Clayton Mizgerd, “Equality in Fill's spectral gap problem”, arXiv:2604.03937 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03937

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2026).

record.title: Dong–Gao–Li–Liu induced rational exponents conjecture
record.statement:
For positive integers $n,s$, let $K_{s,s}$) be the complete bipartite graph with $s$ vertices in each part. For a bipartite graph $H$, let $\mathrm{ex}^*(n,H,s)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing neither a copy of $K_{s,s}$ nor an induced copy of $H$. **Dong–Gao–Li–Liu induced rational exponents conjecture.** For every rational number $r\in(1,2)$, there exist a bipartite graph $H$ and a constant $s_0$ such that

$$
\mathrm{ex}^*(n,H,s)=\Theta_s(n^r)
$$

for any $s\geq s_0$. This is the induced analogue of the rational exponents conjecture for ordinary Turán numbers. The source reports a proof for all $r=2-a/b$ with $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$ and $b\geq\max\{a,(a-1)^2\}$, while the full range of rational exponents in $(1,2)$ remains open.
record.source_name: Tao Jiang and Sean Longbrake, “Induced rational exponents near two”, arXiv:2604.05288 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05288

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2026).

record.title: Erdős–Simonovits rational exponents conjecture
record.statement:
For a graph $H$, let $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $H$. **Erdős–Simonovits rational exponents conjecture.** For every rational number $r\in[1,2]$, there exists a graph $H$ such that

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,H)=\Theta(n^r).
$$

The conjecture asks which rational exponents occur as exact orders of single-graph Turán numbers. The source notes that the result is known for many values of $r$, including the family $r=2-a/b$ with $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$ and $b\geq\max\{a,(a-1)^2\}$, but it is not known in full generality.

record.title: The exact-order conjecture for hypercube saturation
record.statement:
For a positive integer $k$, let $Q_k$ be the $k$-dimensional hypercube viewed as a poset, and let $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,Q_k)$ denote the minimum size of a family of subsets of $[n]$ that is induced-$Q_k$-free but becomes non-free after adding any missing subset.

**Hypercube saturation conjecture.** For every $k\geq 2$,

$$
\operatorname{sat}^*(n,Q_k)=(2^{k-1}-1)n-c,
$$

for some absolute constant $c$.

The paper gives the construction $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,Q_3)\leq 3n-2$ and asks whether it is tight, motivating the proposed formula for all hypercubes. The general equality remains open.
record.source_name: Maria-Romina Ivan and Sean Jaffe, “The Exact Saturation Number for the Diamond”, arXiv:2604.06521 (2026).

record.title: The minimum-degree wheel conjecture
record.statement:
Let $W_{2k}$ be the wheel on $2k+1$ vertices, let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. **Minimum-degree wheel conjecture.** For all integers $n$ and $k$ with $3\leq k<\frac{n}{3}$, if

$$
\delta(G)\geq
\begin{cases}
\left\lfloor\frac{n+k}{2}\right\rfloor, & \text{$k-1$ is odd and $\left\lfloor\frac{n+k}{2}\right\rfloor$ is odd},\\
\left\lceil\frac{n+k}{2}\right\rceil, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
$$

then $W_{2k}\subseteq G$; furthermore, this degree condition is best possible. This is presented as an equivalent formulation of the star–wheel conjecture and would extend the paper’s exact minimum-degree results to the full range $3\leq k<\frac n3$.

record.title: The vertex-minor Ramsey number conjecture for five vertices
record.statement:
Let $R_{\mathrm{vm}}(k)$ denote the smallest integer $n$ such that every graph on $n$ vertices contains the edgeless graph $E_k$ as a vertex-minor. The known values for $k=2,3,4$ are $3$, $7$, and $11$, respectively, and the next unresolved case concerns $k=5$.

**Vertex-minor Ramsey number conjecture for $k=5$.**

$$
R_{\mathrm{vm}}(5)=15.
$$

This is the next unresolved case in the study of vertex-minor Ramsey numbers. It extends the observed pattern $R_{\mathrm{vm}}(k)=4k-5$ for $k=2,3,4$, while the general bounds allow substantially larger values.
record.source_name: Ji Ho Bae, “Vertex-minor Ramsey numbers: exact values and extremal structure”, arXiv:2604.13434 (2026).

record.title: Mader's subdivision conjecture for acyclic digraphs
record.statement:
Let $F$ be an acyclic digraph, and let $\delta^+(D)$ denote the minimum out-degree of a digraph $D$. A **subdivision** of $F$ is obtained by replacing the arcs of $F$ by directed paths with the same endpoints and internally vertex-disjoint interiors. **Mader's subdivision conjecture.** For every acyclic digraph $F$ there exists a number $K=K(F)$ such that every digraph $D$ with

$$
\delta^+(D)\ge K
$$

contains a subdivision of $F$. This remains an open problem concerning degree conditions that force directed subdivisions.
record.source_name: Raphael Steiner, “Openly disjoint cycles and directed tree-width of regular digraphs”, arXiv:2604.13700 (2026).
record.references:
**6 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2603.13955](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.13955), [arXiv:2403.11470](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11470), [arXiv:2008.13224](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13224), [arXiv:1801.08249](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.08249), [arXiv:math/0605178](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605178).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13700

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2026). “Strikingly, the conjecture even remains open when $g=4$, see for the best known partial result in this case.”

record.title: The folklore polynomial diameter conjecture for transitive permutation groups
record.statement:
Let $G\leq S_n$ be a transitive permutation group. The diameter of $G$ is defined using the maximum over generating sets, namely $\operatorname{diam}(G)=\max\{\operatorname{diam}(G,X):X\text{ a generating set for }G\}$. **Folklore conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{diam}(G)\ll n^{O(1)}.
$$

This conjecture concerns polynomial diameter bounds for arbitrary transitive permutation groups. It is attributed to folklore and was made explicit in work of Kornhauser–Miller–Spirakis and McKenzie. The paper notes that it would follow conditionally from Babai’s conjecture and that no transitive permutation group is known with diameter greater than quadratic.
record.source_name: Sean Eberhard, Elena Maini, Luca Sabatini and Gareth Tracey, “Diameter bounds for arbitrary finite groups and applications”, arXiv:2604.15303 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15303

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2026). “This is the best known bound for $\diam(A_n)$, so remains open in this case, as for the other simple groups of unbounded rank.”

record.title: Yokoi's minimum-degree conjecture for odd edge-colorings
record.statement:
There is a constant $d$ such that every $2$-connected graph $G$ of odd order with minimum degree at least $d$ satisfies

$$
\chi'_o(G)\leq 3.
$$

**Yokoi's conjecture.** There exists a constant $d$ satisfying the preceding condition: for every $2$-connected graph $G$ of odd order with minimum degree at least $d$, one has $\chi'_o(G)\leq 3$.

This conjecture is a degree-threshold question for odd edge-colorings of highly connected graphs and is presented as related to the paper's conjecture for $3$-connected graphs. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Mikio Kano, Shun-ichi Maezawa and Kenta Ozeki, “Odd Edge Colorings of Graphs with Odd Order”, arXiv:2604.15824 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15824

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2026).

record.title: Regular bipartite switch-connectivity threshold conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular balanced bipartite graph on $2n$ vertices, and let $f4d8^{\mathbf{connect}}_{k,\mathrm{reg}}(n)$ denote the minimum-degree threshold for the $k$-switch graph of such graphs to be connected. **Regular switch-connectivity threshold conjecture.** There exists $c\geq 0$ such that, for all $n$ and $k$,

$$
\delta^{\mathbf{connect}}_{k,\mathrm{reg}}(n)\in\left[\frac{2n}{k+1}-c,\frac{2n}{k+1}+c\right].
$$

The conjecture predicts that the connectivity threshold is within an additive constant of the degree of the cycle blow-up construction. The source notes that the upper bound is confirmed for $k=2$ and $k=3$, while the lower bound is known when $k+1$ divides $n$.
record.source_name: Ross J. Kang and Clément Legrand-Duchesne, “Dirac's theorem and the switch geometry of perfect matchings”, arXiv:2604.17911 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1906.12235](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.12235).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17911

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2026). “The weaker conjecture obtained by replacing the minimum outdegree condition by having minimum semidegree (minimum of outdegrees and indegrees over all vertices) at least $n/k$ is also still open.”
